content.comment_body: Hello, [user_name], I’m wondering if there’s a way to save data inside a [product_name] module for several days and then later recover the information for analysis. I know real-time logging is possible via PC, but I have multiple devices to handle. The modules I’m using are [article_no] and [article_no] versions. Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Hi, if your goal is to log data and later analyze it on a PC, here are some options: 1) On newer [product_name] modules ([article_no]), you can log to internal memory (limited lines) or to an SD card (more lines). 2) There are solutions discussed in the [product_name] forums like an Excel logger, but for [article_no] or [article_no], separate instances may be needed and a PC has to be connected at all times for this to work. Hope this information helps.
Thank you, [user_name], your explanation helped clarify things for me.
You could try the latest [product_name]Monitor tool. It can monitor, log, and visualize up to 10 [product_name] modules ([article_no]) simultaneously. More info: [url]
On [article_no] modules, only timers and counters remain stored after power cycles.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for solutions to log and retrieve historical operational data from [product_name] modules, but older versions ([article_no], [article_no]) have limited capabilities for onboard data storage and later retrieval for analysis. Only timers and counters retain values on these modules. For more comprehensive data logging, users need either newer hardware or a PC connected at all times, creating a challenge for those who want device autonomy over extended periods.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] modules to autonomously log and store operational data for several days and allow retrieval of this data for analysis, without the need for continuous PC connectivity.
pain_keywords: remnant data only for certain functions
